**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. History, Paper 2 - Cameroon History Since 1800 (0760), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2022. Duration: three hours.**

Instructions to candidates: Candidates are required to answer FOUR questions, choosing at least ONE from each of the sections (Section A: 1800 - 1922; Section B: 1922 - 1961; Section C: 1961 to present). All the questions carry equal marks (25 marks each).

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.
incertitudes: Règle de choix : le sujet impose « answer FOUR questions, choosing at least ONE from each of the sections ». `regles_choix` porte une règle « 1 sur 4 » par section (A : questions 1 à 4, B : 5 à 8, C : 9 à 12), c'est-à-dire le minimum imposé ; la règle « 4 questions en tout » n'est pas exprimable et est recopiée dans `introduction_markdown`.

Points : « All the questions carry equal marks » et chaque question porte 25 marks imprimés (100 points pour les quatre questions à traiter). Aucun écart de points constaté ; `points` vaut 25 pour l'exercice et pour l'unique question de chaque fichier.

Sujet scanné de deux pages (page de garde et questions 1 à 12) ; publicités, filigranes gcerevision.com et texte en transparence du verso (illisible, sans rapport) ignorés ; aucune question coupée, aucune carte ni figure.

Aucun corrigé officiel : les corrigés sont des réponses modèles rédigées au niveau Advanced Level (introduction, développement, conclusion argumentée). Aucune statistique ni citation n'est avancée ; les dates et noms sont donnés de mémoire historique et sont à faire relire par un historien du Cameroun avant mise en ligne.

Les noms de thèmes sont qualifiés (par exemple `foumban conference of 1961`, `cameroon foreign policy under biya`) pour éviter les collisions avec les Tags de l'Histoire francophone ; à recontrôler à l'ingestion avec `find_tag_variant`.

Question 12 : le rétablissement des relations avec Israël (1986), l'adhésion au Commonwealth (1995), l'affaire de Bakassi (saisine de la CIJ en 1994, arrêt du 10 octobre 2002, accord de Greentree de 2006, retrait nigérian en 2008), la CEMAC (1994), le port de Kribi, l'allègement de la dette dans le cadre de l'initiative PPTE (années 2000) et la force régionale contre Boko Haram (depuis 2014) sont cités de mémoire ; le détail chiffré n'est pas donné. Le jugement porté (innovations dans la continuité) est une interprétation.

questions.enonce_markdown:
What major innovations has Paul Biya introduced in Cameroon's foreign policy since 1982?

(25 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** Paul Biya succeeded Ahmadou Ahidjo as President on 6 November 1982. The foreign policy that he inherited was moderate, pro-Western and strongly linked with France, based on non-alignment in principle, good neighbourliness and respect for the Organisation of African Unity (OAU). Biya has kept these basic lines, which reflect Cameroon's dependence on France and the West, but he has introduced a number of innovations, notably the diversification of partners, the restoration of broken relations, the resort to law and arbitration to settle disputes, a more active role in regional organisations and a stress on economic diplomacy. It is better to speak of innovations within continuity than of a complete break.

**1. Diversification of diplomatic and economic partners**
- Biya extended Cameroon's relations beyond France and the Western world to Asia and other regions, especially China, Japan, India and other emerging countries, as well as the Arab world. Chinese loans and companies became important in infrastructure, for example in the construction of the Kribi deep-sea port. This reduced Cameroon's dependence on a single partner, though France remained an essential partner.

**2. Re-establishment of relations with Israel**
- Cameroon had broken relations with Israel after the 1973 war, in line with the position of many African states. In 1986 Biya's government restored diplomatic relations with Israel, a pragmatic decision to open the country to technology, security cooperation and a wider range of partners, and a departure from the policy of his predecessor.

**3. Entry into the Commonwealth (1995)**
- In 1995 Cameroon, a country with a French-based majority, was admitted to the Commonwealth, a decision which was unusual because Cameroon had no British colonial history except in the former Southern Cameroons. It was meant to gain new economic and diplomatic ties, to meet the concerns of the Anglophone population, and to balance Cameroon's membership of La Francophonie. Cameroon thus became a member of both the Commonwealth and the Francophone community.

**4. Peaceful and legal settlement of the Bakassi dispute**
- After border clashes with Nigeria in the early 1980s and again in the 1990s over the Bakassi peninsula, Cameroon took the dispute to the International Court of Justice in 1994 instead of resorting to war. The Court's judgment of 10 October 2002 recognised Cameroon's sovereignty over Bakassi, and the Greentree Agreement of 2006, mediated by the United Nations, led to the withdrawal of the Nigerian administration and troops in 2008. This was an important innovation, because it made the legal route and international mediation the basic method of solving border disputes, and it has often been cited as a model for Africa.

**5. Active participation in regional and multilateral organisations**
- Biya's Cameroon has played an active role in Central African regional institutions: the creation of the Central African Economic and Monetary Community (CEMAC, 1994) to replace UDEAC, the Economic Community of Central African States (ECCAS), the Gulf of Guinea Commission and the Lake Chad Basin Commission (founded in 1964), and in the African Union. It has contributed to regional peace efforts, particularly in the Central African Republic, and in the regional force against Boko Haram in the Lake Chad basin since 2014, in cooperation with Nigeria, Chad and Niger.
- Cameroon has also participated in UN activities, including peacekeeping.

**6. Economic and development diplomacy**
- Since the economic crisis of the late 1980s and the devaluation of the CFA franc in 1994, foreign policy has been used to obtain aid, debt relief and investment, as with the agreements with the IMF and World Bank and the debt cancellation under the Heavily Indebted Poor Countries initiative in the 2000s, and to attract partners for infrastructure. This marks a shift from the political emphasis of the Ahidjo years towards a pragmatic, economy-oriented diplomacy.

**7. Limits and continuity.** Many features have not changed: the close links with France, military and economic cooperation, Cameroon's membership of the Franc Zone, a cautious and low-profile style and a rejection of confrontation. Critics note that Biya's diplomacy is often reactive and personalised, and that domestic crises, notably the Anglophone crisis and Boko Haram, have damaged Cameroon's image abroad.

**Conclusion.** Since 1982 Paul Biya has introduced significant innovations in Cameroon's foreign policy: the diversification of partners, the restoration of relations with Israel, entry into the Commonwealth, the settlement of the Bakassi dispute through law and mediation, greater regional involvement and an emphasis on economic diplomacy. These changes have been made within a framework of continuity with the moderate, pro-Western policy of Ahidjo.
